label: traxary
description: The tracker platform traxary runs on. Its operators run more than one site on the same codebase, so the endpoint, auth and field map live here rather than in each tracker def — a change reaching all of them is then a single edit.
notes:
BETA/TESTING TYPE — not part of a release, and must be held back together with the tracker defs on this platform (traxary, peergarden). Shipping it alone would put a Traxary option in every user's type picker for a platform that is not live yet.

The key is FINAL: Traxary is the platform's own name, confirmed 2026-09-03. This is not the situation renamedTrackerTypes exists for — "gazelle" was adopted as a generic base for forks that each went their own way, whereas here we work directly with the platform's developer, who is willing to add endpoints where Yata needs them. One codebase, one set of field names, one type.

Platform facts that belong here rather than in a tracker def: /api/user is Bearer-authenticated and reports no join date, so api.required_fields demands one at setup; and the response nests everything under stats/events/*group objects.

GROUP LADDERS COME FROM THE TRACKER, not from a def — group_api above, and GROUP_API_PLAN.md. That is why the spec sits on the TYPE while events and extended_stats sit on tracker defs: whether one UNIT3D install exposes an endpoint says nothing about the next, but serving /api/user/groups is a property of this platform. A traxary site nobody has written a def for still gets a working ladder, and a site that would rather not publish its mechanics to non-members can support Yata anyway — the endpoint is authenticated, and a def file in a public repo is not. Tracker defs on this platform must therefore ship NO "groups" array: a build-time copy is precisely the thing being replaced.

The response carries four ladders (auto/upload/internal/premium) where Yata models one; "ladder": "auto" picks the one progression is measured against, matching autogroup driving the badge while uploadgroup/internalgroup stay display-only fields. Requirement values arrive raw — bytes for upload/seedsize, seconds for age/avg_seedtime, plain counts otherwise — and the unit is inferred from the Yata field each maps to, so the map states only WHERE a requirement goes. A type the map does not name is dropped rather than guessed at.

Not yet served per group by /api/user/groups: color, icon and perks (the site's own Groups & Roles page renders all three, and the premium ladder already carries perks, so the shape is there). Yata reads them from that endpoint when present, so they need no Yata change when the platform adds them — still worth asking the dev for, in that order.

Meanwhile /api/user DOES carry the style of the rank the user currently holds, which is why autogroup.color/icon map to group_color/group_icon above. Those are overlaid onto the matching rung of the ladder, so the badge, the styled username and the perk icons all light up for the group you are in. It only ever styles that one rung — nothing else can be known from a field describing your own rank — and it never overrides a style the ladder itself supplies, so it silently stops mattering the day /api/user/groups serves colours.

Three concurrent memberships are reported (autogroup, uploadgroup, internalgroup) where Yata models one ladder. autogroup drives the group badge and progression; the other two are carried as display-only fields. Deliberately unresolved: it is the only platform we have seen do it, and it is pre-launch, so the group model is left alone until it is worth changing.

The field map is what Traxary's beta instance actually served. PeerGarden's /api namespace answers but has no user route yet (see its def), so this type is written to the shape we KNOW works — when the endpoint lands there the tracker def should simply start reporting, with no further change on either side. If a site on this platform ever genuinely diverges, that is what a tracker-level api block is for.

scrape.disable_scraping is NOT set here. It records an operator's request about a particular site, so it stays in each tracker def even when the same people run both.
